title: Hannibal: the person and the accounts that remain
purpose: Preserve a walkable path from a famous historical-person label back to bounded surviving source reports while keeping mediation, source dependence and unknowns visible.

subject.identity_ceiling: The entity is a thin routing anchor. Source-literal mentions remain separately inspectable and candidate-linked; the record does not turn the surviving biography into the person.

selection.selected_for: Historical-person source-survival and source-dependence stress case after the first three public records tested artwork provenance, repeated-claim ancestry and living-practice transmission.
selection.boundary: Selection did not establish representativeness, historical priority, importance or entitlement. Publication followed bounded source/reader review and current-validator compatibility checks; reader benefit remains unestablished.
selection.selection_history_ceiling: No selection-time candidate pool or alternatives list is preserved from the pre-publication selection process; do not reconstruct one after the fact.

notes: Thin routing anchor for the historical human conventionally called Hannibal Barca; exact dates, appearance, routes and biographical details are not identity-key material.

The checked Nepos Latin passage attests the literal string 'Hannibal'. The checked Polybius English reading surface renders the name as 'Hannibal'; a separate Perseus Greek-edition passage-token check at 3.33.17-18 attests the Greek form 'Ἀννίβας' in both sections. The fuller modern display label remains conventional rather than claimed as source-attested by every checked surface.
Two public source-literal mentions remain candidate-linked rather than silently upgraded into identity certainty.

scope.ceiling: Nepos reports that Silenus and Sosylus were with Hannibal and wrote about the war; THR has not inspected their complete works.

object.literal: Polybius dismisses the authority of Sosylus and Chaereas.

scope.ceiling: This is Polybius' evaluation of another historian, not THR's adjudication of Sosylus.

object.literal: A bronze tablet at the Lacinian promontory carrying Hannibal's troop lists.

scope.ceiling: Polybius reports finding and using the bronze tablet described at 3.33.17-18. THR has not observed that ancient carrier or an independently preserved copy, and this fixture does not establish that it is physically identical to the column/inscription described at 3.56.4.

subject.literal: Polybius' claimed investigation of the Alpine crossing

object.literal: Polybius says he questioned men who had been present, inspected the country, and crossed the Alps himself.

scope.ceiling: This records Polybius' own account of his evidence-gathering method. THR did not observe the reported interviews, route inspection, travel, or ancient investigation.

object.literal: Hannibal crossed the Alps into Italy.

scope.ceiling: Attribution to Polybius' surviving account; exact pass and complete source ancestry are not established by this fixture.

source_relationships.current_aperture: Greek/Roman-mediated and incomplete; includes one bounded Greek-edition token check for Polybius 3.33.17-18

current_findings: Two bounded ancient-text reading surfaces make attributed reports about Hannibal and their own source world inspectable.
Polybius' reports about a Lacinium tablet and his own investigative method remain reports by Polybius, not direct THR observations.
Nepos attests Silenus and Sosylus as companions/historians; their complete works are not represented as inspected THR source objects.
The checked aperture is asymmetric and incomplete; later repetition is not counted as independent corroboration by default.

A Perseus Greek-edition passage-token check attests the form 'Ἀννίβας' at Polybius 3.33.17 and 3.33.18; this narrows the source-literal boundary only and is not manuscript verification or identity proof.
unknowns: A complete source genealogy among Polybius, Livy and other surviving writers.
The full Punic/Carthaginian documentary aperture and all surviving fragments.
Whether the Lacinium tablet described at 3.33 and column/inscription at 3.56 are the same physical carrier.
The exact Alpine pass and many other biographical/historical disputes outside this record.
Manuscript-level verification and full passage-level Greek critical-text inspection beyond the bounded 3.33.17-18 token check.
